title: This Cancer Kills Children in a Year. Research Has Been Stalled for a Year.
summary: For 27 years, the Pediatric Brain Tumor Consortium worked to save kids with brain cancer. But just before 5-year-old Ryleigh Schecter was diagnosed, the government shut it down.

When Ryleigh Schecter answered the front door to her home, she was wearing an oversized lavender bow in her hair that matched the stripes on her shirt. “Rainbow” is her favorite color, she told me as I sat with her and her parents, Amanda and Aaron, in their cozy living room in Twinsburg, Ohio. To prove it, she recited the colors of the spectrum in order, adding “pink, silver, gold” at the end. She is 5.


Eventually, the Schecters and I began to talk about the medicine she takes, and on cue Ryleigh sped to the kitchen and raced back with a sandwich bag full of Skittles. It contained only the red, orange and yellow ones. “I don’t like the purple or the green,” she explained.


Ryleigh takes two drugs every night, one designed to treat breast cancer. Her mother mixes them as if from a chemistry set and administers them orally with a syringe. Ryleigh hates them.


“The first one tastes disgusting, and the second one tastes medium,” Ryleigh told me.


What does the first one taste like? I asked her.


“Dirty water mixed together,” she replied. After each dose, Ryleigh eats a Skittle to wash away the taste. She likes orange best.


Image


Amanda Schecter, Ryleigh’s mother, administering one of Ryleigh’s drugs that she mixes in a syringe.
